output.summary: Added software prefetching to the hash-join paths in src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp. Prefetching is only a hint and the logic is unchanged, so results are identical. (1) In ProbeForPointersInternal, before the main loop, a pass prefetches entries[hashes_dense[i] & bitmask] for every probe row. (2) In GetRowPointersInternal, before row_matcher_build.Match, a pass prefetches the row pointers for keys_to_compare_sel. (3) In InsertHashesLoop, before each probing round, the target entries are prefetched for writing. All three are guarded by GCC/Clang and run only when capacity*sizeof(ht_entry_t) is above a fixed 1MB (L2-scale) constant. The build passes and results check out. Bench on q09 against the current best, four runs: -5.7% and -4.8% with probe prefetch only (1)+(2); then -9.9% and -5.6% after adding the build prefetch (3).
output.generality: Helps any hash join whose pointer table is larger than about 1MB, meaning build sides of roughly 128K+ rows (fact-to-fact joins, large dimensions, large intermediates). It speeds up both probing and building. Small hash tables skip the extra passes because of the size guard. On compilers other than GCC/Clang nothing changes. The worst case is probes that are already cache-friendly, where you pay an extra loop of up to 2048 iterations per vector.
output.notes: The gain is real but modest (about 5-10% on q09) and close to the noise bar. Out-of-order execution apparently already overlaps some of the misses. Prefetching for the whole vector at once is crude: it issues up to 2048 prefetches, more than the hardware can keep in flight. A possible next step is distance-based prefetching inside the loop (prefetch i+16 while processing i), which could do better. The build-side prefetch added visible gain, so the build phase matters for q09 as well. A separate idea that was not tried: prefetching chained rows in ScanStructure::Next/AdvancePointers for chains longer than one.
